steps.title: Title
steps.say: Seasons come from how Earth is tilted as it travels around the Sun.

steps.title: The Sun
steps.say: The Sun gives off light and heat that reach the whole Earth.

steps.title: Tilted Earth
steps.say: Earth's axis is tilted about 23.4 degrees, and it stays tilted the same way all year.

steps.title: Sunlight
steps.say: Sunlight travels to Earth in nearly parallel rays.

steps.title: Northern Summer
steps.say: When the Northern Hemisphere leans toward the Sun, its light is more direct and its days are longer.

ops.text: Northern summer: tilted toward the Sun

steps.title: Winter
steps.say: Six months later, the Northern Hemisphere leans away, so its light is spread out and its days are shorter.

ops.text: Northern winter: tilted away from the Sun

steps.title: Not Distance
steps.say: Distance is not the cause. Earth is actually closest to the Sun in January.

ops.text: Not distance: Earth is closest to the Sun in January.
